hints.title: Class Enrollment Aggregation
hints.text: The table records student enrollments across distinct courses. How can you group enrollment records by academic course and filter for courses that contain at least five enrolled students?

hints.title: Course Size Invariant
hints.text: Grouping by course name consolidates student enrollments into singular course aggregates whose size can be filtered with a post-aggregation clause.

hints.title: Group By Course Having Procedure
hints.text: Group the Courses records by class name. Filter using a having clause where count of student is at least five, and select the class column.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT class
FROM Courses
GROUP BY class
HAVING COUNT(student) >= 5;
```

complexity.notes: Single pass group by aggregation with having count filter.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all student rows repeatedly for each distinct class takes O(C * N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Group by with having aggregates courses in O(N) time with O(C) memory for course buckets.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Properly grouping by class; filtering with having count >= 5.

solutions.code:
SELECT class
FROM Courses
GROUP BY class
HAVING COUNT(student) >= 5;

FROM Courses
GROUP BY class
HAVING COUNT(student) >= 5;

import pandas as pd

def find_classes(courses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    counts = courses.groupby('class').size().reset_index(name='count')
    return counts[counts['count'] >= 5][['class']]
